faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: Below you will find answers to the most common questions about your rental contract, service and warranties. Can't find your question? Feel free to contact us.

q1.question: Can I cancel early?
q1.answer: Cancelling during the ongoing term is generally not possible; a fixed contract period applies that ends automatically once the term is over. If you concluded the agreement remotely (online or by phone), you do have a statutory 14-day cooling-off period, as long as the installation has not yet been placed. The exact conditions are stated in your rental agreement. Contact us so we can review your specific situation.

q2.question: What happens after the rental term?
q2.answer: When your rental term ends you have three options: you can take over the installation at its residual value, continue renting at a reduced rate, or have the panels removed free of charge. We contact you well before your contract ends to go through the options. Unsure which choice suits you? Contact us.

q3.question: How do I submit a service request?
q3.answer: You submit a service request easily through our contact form; select the "Service request" category. Describe as clearly as possible what you have noticed — ideally within 14 days of noticing it — so we can help you faster. We respond within 5 business days. Do you have an urgent fault? Please mention this in your message.

q4.question: Which warranties apply?
q4.answer: Throughout the term of your rental agreement we repair defects, faults and damage to the installation, so it keeps meeting reasonable requirements. In addition, the manufacturer's warranty applies to the panels and the inverter, among other things. The exact periods and coverage differ per component and are set out in your agreement; when in doubt, contact us.

q5.question: How long will my system last?
q5.answer: Solar panels last 25 to 30 years on average and usually keep generating power afterwards, albeit at a gradually declining yield. The inverter typically has a shorter lifespan and may be replaced once during the term. Questions about the condition of your system? Contact us.

q6.question: What happens if I sell my house?
q6.answer: When you sell your home the rental contract can in most cases be transferred to the new owner, so the installation can simply stay in place. We guide you and the buyer through this transfer. Let us know in good time once a sale is on the horizon, and we will arrange the transfer smoothly. Contact us to start the transfer.
